newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks steady at start after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: German stocks steady at start after jobs data.

text.p: German shares opened steady on Thursday, shrugging off a small rise in German jobless data for August but with buying limited before today's Bundesbank meeting and Friday's U.S. jobs figures.
The blue-chip DAX index of shares was scarcely changed at 2,532.66 just after its open, with the IBIS index, which tracks all-day electronic trade, 6.83 points, or 0.27 percent, higher at 2,533.01.
Dealers said news of a 14,000 rise in German unemployment in August compared to the month before had been largely expected.
"A particularly good unemployment figure could have influenced the debt market (and then indirectly share trading) but these figures were already largely discounted," one trader said.

With the Bundesbank widely expected to leave its key interest rates unchanged, dealers said stock levels were expected to stay around the same levels until U.S. jobs data gave further indications of the likely direction for U.S. interest rates.

Corporate news was thin. Diversified industrial Preussag was traded seven marks lower at 349 on IBIS on dealer talk of downgrades following news on Wednesday of a fall in sales for the first nine months of the year.
